quest.title: Project Moongazer
quest.description: During your previous adventures, you have learned some very important secrets indeed. Yet the mysteries surrounding Project Moongazer and Ninnin have not yet come undone, and so, you decide to check out the final stop on this trip...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x300, Primogem x40, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x3

talks.objective: Take the plunge into Moonheart Chasm

dialogues.speaker: Terminal
dialogues.text: ...Unable to... accurately pinpoint your coordinates... I cannot know how long... this reply reaches you...

dialogues.speaker: Terminal
dialogues.text: ...But I'd like to... respond... at this very moment...

dialogues.speaker: Terminal
dialogues.text: ...We are travelers... who have traversed the universe alone for a long time... and your voices... it is as if a bonfire has suddenly lit up a dark forest...

dialogues.speaker: Terminal
dialogues.text: ...You take great risks... yet you are fearless... You inspire us and warm our hearts...

dialogues.speaker: Terminal
dialogues.text: ...I believe... in this moment... it is the gravity of the starry sea and destiny... that connects you and me...

dialogues.speaker: Terminal
dialogues.text: ...In the future... we will try... to find your... planet... but not now, unfortunately... We're still dealing with... some trouble...

dialogues.speaker: Terminal
dialogues.text: (...A burst of signal static...)

dialogues.speaker: Terminal
dialogues.text: #{M#...Aether! Are you ready?}{F#...Lumine, how're we doing?}

dialogues.speaker: Terminal
dialogues.text: #{M#...One moment, Lumine...}{F#...Almost ready, Aether...}

dialogues.speaker: Terminal
dialogues.text: (...A burst of signal static...)

dialogues.speaker: Terminal
dialogues.text: ...Well then... My regards to you...

dialogues.speaker: Terminal
dialogues.text: ...Just as you said, the sea of stars is vast and boundless, and we are not alone...

dialogues.speaker: Terminal
dialogues.text: ...Let us meet again beneath the starry skies...

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: We made it down.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is this the moon's core?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: No, that's still up ahead. With you coming along, we'll have to enter it the normal way.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: As for this place... it is the masterpiece of that Dragon Lord of Darkness

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: He reforged the moon into a terrifying weapon, and this is its launch silo.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: The lunar core, the source of the moon's power, became artillery fire aimed at Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: However, that primordial ruler ultimately met defeat at the hands of the Heavenly Principles. This place is no longer a threat.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Let's continue on.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Beneath this door is where we need to go.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Looks like we'll need a key to open it.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: You already have it with you.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: This is Lusalim's final facility — the one before was the Lunar Veil Laboratory, which is now the lunar sea.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You mean the Ancient Moon's Fount?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: That's the one.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Hmm? Has the system detected us?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Regardless, they can do nothing to stop us.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Maagees has already picked Paimon and Ninnin up and is heading back. We can get going once you're ready.

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: Then let's go.

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: Alright. Still, we shouldn't delay for too long.

talks.objective: Take the plunge into Moonheart Chasm
Open the way to the moon's core

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: We're back.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Columbina! Looks like things went just dandy for you two at the moon's core, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We did indeed learn a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? So you know where Eggie came from, and what Project Moongazer's all about?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Yes, and the key to unlock the Moongazer module — it's all right here.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: I'll hand it over to you now, Ninnin.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Once you've read the information here, you'll know what your mission is.

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: Thank you! I have been waiting for this moment.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Columbina? {NICKNAME}? Why do you two look so serious?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Because her mission involves unknown risks.

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: What kind of risks?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: You'll find out by the time you're done reading.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's a little confused... What exactly is Eggie's mission?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As Eggie reads the information, you tell Paimon everything.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sending a message into the starry sky? So that's what Project Moongazer's all about...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So the risk is... we could expose Teyvat? Are you serious? This... Ugh, this is a tough call...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eggie... are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, don't be sad! We can still talk this over, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Remember those snacks? We can split 'em fifty-fifty, no problem!

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: No, I'm not sad.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But you're crying!

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: I'm not sad. And I'm not crying. This is just... just...

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: A toast to those who came before.

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: #Columbina, {NICKNAME}, Paimon. Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: You're my friends. I don't want to make things difficult for you, so I'm willing to... give up on my mission.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eggie...

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: It's okay, Paimon. I'm not the first to have executed this plan.

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: My predecessors have long since sent our voices out into the stars.

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: Those voices, so filled with courage, must have traveled to the farthest reaches of the starry skies by now.

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: As long as those voices endure, silence cannot reign across the universe, and that is enough.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}... have you made up your mind?

choices.text: Maybe we could execute Project Moongazer one last time.

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: I agree.

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: Y—You really think so?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Can we really take that risk?

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: Moongazer has already been executed many times.

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: The false sky used to conceal Teyvat has also been opened more than once.

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: The Frost Moon has existed outside the false sky for thousands of years. Yet even now, there are no traces of Abyssal corruption here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh? You mean this might not be as dangerous as we thought?

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: There are many possibilities. Perhaps the Abyss isn't constantly watching this place, or perhaps the great ruler of the firmament has taken other measures...

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: And to minimize risks, I will also use my power as the Moon Goddess to shield any message that Ninnin might send.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What does that mean?

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: Kuuvahki and the ancient moon's energy are both, in essence, the power of the Light Realm. As such, I can infuse my power into the transmitted messages.

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: Once the data passes through the false sky, I can also use that same power to monitor the surrounding area.

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: If there's danger, I can erase the information. That way, we won't be discovered.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh? That sounds great! But... can you maintain your power the whole time?

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: Well, my strength does have limits. I can only keep it going up to a certain distance.

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: I will try to shield the message as far as possible. At that point, its source will not be so easily traced.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That sounds more feasible.

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: But... will this hurt you?

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: Don't worry. We have the support of an entire moon here, you know.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, are you ready, Eggie? Once you've made up your mind, there'll be no turning back!

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: ...Can I ask one more question?

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: Yes?

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: Why would you do all this for me?

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: Because we're friends.

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: That's it?

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: Yes. That's all the reason I need.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: P—Paimon does, too!

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: I understand. Then, I am ready.

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: I was born for this moment.

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: Alright. Now, sing out toward the stars. Teyvat's moonlight shall send you off on your voyage.

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: Uhm... Hello... Hello, everyone!

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: I am so glad... to be able to send this message out into the mysterious vastness of space...

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: I don't know if it will reach you... But, if nothing else, let it at least dispel some of the silence that fills this cold universe.

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: If "you" are out there and you hear this, then there must surely be some kind of special gravity that, like the moon, has captured us both.

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: So, I'd like you and your civilization to know... that you are not alone beneath this boundless starry sky.

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: Our era is drawing to a close... but our courage, faith, and intellect will echo across the sea of stars... via this tiny message.

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: It is insignificant, but it is our light... I hope it emboldens you. You do not face the unknown and the darkness alone.

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: Please keep sending your voices out into the stars, and let them become your light too.

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: A single ray of light is feeble, easily swallowed by the darkness, but as long as another light shines out before it can fade...

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: Then one day, there will surely come a ray of light that pierces the night like the dawn.

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: Last but not least... we are... Mo{RUBY#[S]starry sky}ongazers in an unremarkable corner of the universe...

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: Our names are...

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: Ibni-Belum...

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: Ungien...

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: Maagees-Geti...

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: Lusalim...

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: Nin-Kiggia...

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: To everyone who can hear this... We send you our regards...

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: My friends... Thank you... Let us meet again... beneath the starry skies...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eggie has completed her mission...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Her hat...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Are you okay, Columbina?

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: I'm fine. But I need to stay focused for what comes next, since I'll be pushing my strength to its limits.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then let's hurry and find a quiet place!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Goodbye, Eggie... Paimon will always remember you.

response.speaker: Terminal
response.text: (...A burst of signal static...)

response.speaker: Terminal
response.text: (...It seems the activation of the Moongazer module has activated a sealed data segment...)

response.speaker: Terminal
response.text: ...This is... the ...

response.speaker: Terminal
response.text: ...Received... message... and... sending our reply...

choices.text: I send you all my regards.
It's unfortunate, but we can't take the risk.

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: And what if I could use my power as the Moon Goddess to shield the messages that Ninnin sends?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What does that mean?

talks.objective: Open the way to the moon's core

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Our journey has reached its end. She is the key to activating Project Moongazer.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: An imprint left here by the project's final inheritor.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: She will explain everything.
Hey! Hello there.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hello?

dialogues.speaker: Nin-Kiggia's Mark
dialogues.text: I'm Nin-Kiggia. You can call me Ninnin. That's what people usually call me.

dialogues.speaker: Nin-Kiggia's Mark
dialogues.text: What's your name? Ibni-Belum? Ungien? Maagees? Or are you Lusalim?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #I'm {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Nin-Kiggia's Mark
dialogues.text: Hehe, no need to answer me. Unfortunately, I'm no longer here. This is just a recording.

dialogues.speaker: Nin-Kiggia's Mark
dialogues.text: But if you look at it another way, it's not "unfortunate" at all. You're here, and that means the plan was a success — you have inherited our mission.

dialogues.speaker: Nin-Kiggia's Mark
dialogues.text: You must still be very confused about a great number of things, such as — "Who exactly am I?"

dialogues.speaker: Nin-Kiggia's Mark
dialogues.text: Let me tell you: You are a new life created through the will of the moon, a crucial part of Project Moongazer.

dialogues.speaker: Nin-Kiggia's Mark
dialogues.text: "And what exactly is this project?" you must be thinking... Don't worry, I'll get to that.

dialogues.speaker: Nin-Kiggia's Mark
dialogues.text: First, please thank the Three Moon Sisters, who permitted our transgression and allowed us to borrow the power of creation from the moon's very origin.

dialogues.speaker: Nin-Kiggia's Mark
dialogues.text: Secondly, thanks are owed to my teacher, Lusalim. He inherited everyone's research and successfully collated all their ancient moon energy data.

dialogues.speaker: Nin-Kiggia's Mark
dialogues.text: That's how I was able to gather that data in this sea at the moon's core. Then, when the primordial power of creation was triggered... "Bam!"—

dialogues.speaker: Nin-Kiggia's Mark
dialogues.text: A cute little black kuuhenki — namely you — was born.

dialogues.speaker: Nin-Kiggia's Mark
dialogues.text: You might inherit the name of someone who came before us through the ocean of data, or you might not, but you will probably recall that you have a mission.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So this is how Eggie was born...

dialogues.speaker: Nin-Kiggia's Mark
dialogues.text: Next, we must say thank you to Madam Maagees, who uncovered the nature of our astral visitor — a data-based lifeform. Her research was the foundation upon which you were born.

dialogues.speaker: Nin-Kiggia's Mark
dialogues.text: And we have Ungien, who sacrificed his life to relay the final message that our guest's civilization sent out into the stars.

dialogues.speaker: Nin-Kiggia's Mark
dialogues.text: Then came the first Moongazer, Ibni-Belum, who led us to the moon, opened our eyes, and tirelessly gazed into the brilliant starry skies.

dialogues.speaker: Nin-Kiggia's Mark
dialogues.text: Finally, dear successor, thank you as well for your imminent sacrifice, which will activate the final step of our project.

dialogues.speaker: Nin-Kiggia's Mark
dialogues.text: Your mission is to continue transmitting the message we once received out into the universe.

dialogues.speaker: Nin-Kiggia's Mark
dialogues.text: "A single ray of light is feeble, easily swallowed by the darkness, but as long as another light shines out before it can fade..."

dialogues.speaker: Nin-Kiggia's Mark
dialogues.text: "Then one day, there will surely come a ray of light that pierces the night like the dawn."

dialogues.speaker: Nin-Kiggia's Mark
dialogues.text: I imagine you understand what I mean at this point, yes? As it happens, my time is almost up... But that's okay. I'll be joining them all soon.

dialogues.speaker: Nin-Kiggia's Mark
dialogues.text: Come to think of it, you might actually have inherited my name, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Nin-Kiggia's Mark
dialogues.text: It's time to say goodbye. Go complete your mission. And lastly... I salute you, and all your fellow Mo{RUBY#[S]starry sky}ongazers.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: And that's everything.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: All the researchers who once explored the starry sky have had their data merged into this ocean. By the will of the moon, they will be reborn at some point in the future in forms akin to Eggie's.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: They will instinctively consume each other to acquire more data until the mission becomes clear in their minds.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Then they will walk the path we have walked once more, come here, and learn everything.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: They will use themselves as keys to open the Moongazer module in the Eye of Ibni-Belum, and resend the message out into the universe.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Then, they will return to the cycle of life...

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Yes, and this cycle may have already happened more than once.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: That said, calling out into unknown space is not necessarily safe.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: The dragon researchers must have also realized this, which is why they began work on the Lunar Veil.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: And in Ninnin's era, the world already teetered on the brink of destruction due to the conflict between two supreme beings.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: But peace has been restored in Teyvat, at least for now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (If the signal sent out this time ends up drawing the attention of the darkness that dwells amidst the stars to this place...)

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: As promised, I will hand the key and the message over to Ninnin.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: But do you think we should stop her from completing her mission? Or should we support her?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I need some time to think.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Mmhmm, I understand. Then let us return to the first Moongazer's tower.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What about Paimon and Ninnin?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Don't worry. Maagees will pick them up.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: It'll be a fairly long journey. We'll have plenty of time to give this some more thought.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Let's go. It's time to leave.
